surfaces.name: Corgi terminal UI (Ghostty-powered viewer for a persistent runtime)
corgi command line, scripting and JSON RPC
Corgi daemon (persistent runtime that owns panes and agents)

claims.answer: A terminal application for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (amd64, arm64) that runs inside the user's terminal; remote use is ssh -t host corgi; no native Windows, browser or phone client; no editor extension.

scope.version: stable release 20261106T233845Z-03c72b717526 (commit 03c72b7, 2026-11-06); default-branch work at c29ecae (2026-11-11) is noted separately

desktop_os.answer: README install offers macOS Apple Silicon and Linux amd64/arm64 builds; no Windows build. Corgi runs in a host terminal rather than as a separate GUI app.

mobile_apps.answer: No iOS or Android app; the install section lists only macOS and Linux.

browser.answer: No browser client in the released product (a browser viewer appears only as a future note in the unreleased design doc).

mobile_browser.answer: No browser client, so no phone browser access.

cli.answer: corgi command with scripting, headless, watch, usage and rpc commands.

editor_extensions.answer: No editor extension in the repository.

task_actions.answer: Start agents from the picker, message or send input, read panes, review changes, jump to waiting agents, resume closed agents.

notifications.answer: Sounds and unread/needs-input indicators in the UI; over SSH only the terminal bell; no push notifications.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Detaching leaves the runtime running so a later corgi (or ssh -t host corgi) reattaches; there is no multi-device client.

limitations: Windows is not offered by the installer; there is no browser or phone client; SSH machine profiles exist only on the default branch.

evidence.title: README.md
evidence.finding: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer for humans and agents powered by Ghostty; install script for macOS Apple Silicon or Linux amd64/arm64; detects claude, codex, pi, opencode and omp panes, installs hooks, shows status, subagents, usage, rename/fork, resume after crash, multiple accounts; corgi list/tab/pane/message/read scripting; MIT.

evidence.title: LICENSE
evidence.finding: MIT License, copyright Tal Shiri and Corgi contributors; notification sounds from herdr remain Apache-2.0.

evidence.title: docs/reference.md
evidence.locator: Set up and import; Tabs and panes; Review changes; Ask Corgi; Script Corgi; Settings and troubleshooting
evidence.finding: Setup and import from tmux, herdr, cmux; tabs, panes and workspaces; review panel; Ask Corgi prompt with memory; scripting commands; state under ~/.local/state/corgi; remote work by running ssh -t host corgi so detaching leaves the runtime on that host.

evidence.title: docs/agents.md
evidence.locator: Providers; Conversation ownership; Children, usage and context; Inference and data boundaries
evidence.finding: Each provider is an adapter (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Oh My Pi) with hooks or extensions; daemon owns a conversation actor per provider session; children and usage are observed; summary inference uses a private worker whose provider can differ from the observed agent.

evidence.title: docs/agent-launcher.md
evidence.locator: Start an agent; Several accounts; YOLO
evidence.finding: Agent picker starts or resumes agents; each provider can have several accounts (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME folders) with usage; per-provider YOLO checkbox off by default.

evidence.title: docs/workspaces.md
evidence.locator: Follow activity; Hibernate; Create or choose a worktree; Browse and compare worktrees
evidence.finding: Workspace indicators for working, needs input, unread; jump to attention; hibernate and archive; create a git worktree from the agent picker; browse and compare worktrees; push unpushed commits.

evidence.title: docs/releases.md
evidence.finding: Publisher builds macOS arm64 and Linux amd64/arm64, signs a manifest, serves it from https://corgi.computer; releases are not published on GitHub; test builds do not send crash reports; optional Sentry.

evidence.title: assets/help.txt
evidence.finding: corgi start/attach, open, onboard, update with rollback, hooks, integration, account, headless start/list/send/events/stop, watch --json, usage --json, rpc, reload, checkpoint, shutdown, bugreport; workspaces group tabs and panes, no worktrees note.

evidence.title: assets/corgi-skill.md
evidence.finding: corgi --skill prints agent instructions: list, tab and pane commands, message agents, pane read, grep conversations, headless sessions, usage.

evidence.title: HACKING.md
evidence.finding: Zig native layer with Ghostty, Bun TypeScript daemon and viewer; release builds configured with Sentry report daemon and viewer crashes; development builds have no DSN.

evidence.title: src/telemetry.ts
evidence.finding: Opt-in aggregate timings and a bounded timeline written locally, enabled by CORGI_TELEMETRY; no network I/O in the module.

evidence.title: src/crash.ts
evidence.finding: Crash reporter uploads to a Sentry DSN only when a release build sets one (src/build_config.ts default is empty).

evidence.title: scripts/install.sh.in
evidence.finding: Installer script served at corgi.computer/install.sh for macOS Apple Silicon and Linux.

evidence.title: src/providers.ts
evidence.finding: Provider adapters registered in UI order: claude, codex, pi, opencode, omp.

evidence.title: docs/remote.md
evidence.finding: Default-branch (not in stable release 03c72b7) documentation for corgi machine add and --machine: each machine keeps its own daemon; no Corgi network listener, account service or hosted relay.

evidence.title: docs/remote-sandbox.md
evidence.finding: Default-branch simulated remote lab for development.

evidence.title: src
evidence.locator: bounded search at 03c72b7 of src/, docs/ and native/: saml, oidc, sso, rbac, organization, schedule, cron, webhook, gh pr create, spend limit, rollback, issue tracker
evidence.finding: Bounded search found no SSO or role model, no scheduler or webhook trigger, no pull-request creation, no issue tracker and no spend cap setting.

evidence.title: GitHub repository metadata
evidence.finding: 206 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-11-15, homepage corgi.computer; no GitHub releases, only test tags.

evidence.title: stable channel manifest
evidence.locator: stable channel manifest|payload version and commit
evidence.finding: Signed stable channel manifest names version 20261106T233845Z-03c72b717526 at commit 03c72b7175269a6b4f0c2b3451202c462f72aa3e with macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 builds (Linux arm64 on its own channel).

evidence.title: Corgi home page
evidence.finding: Prerendered product page with install command; no pricing page; the README hero image URL https://corgi.computer/images/hero.gif returned 404 at retrieval.

evidence.title: docs/images/localization/ru-review.png
evidence.finding: First-party capture of the Corgi UI with sidebar workspaces, an agent list and the review panel.

changes.summary: Initial full-profile source pass of tals/corgi at the stable release 20261106T233845Z-03c72b717526 (commit 03c72b7, advertised by https://corgi.computer/channels/stable.json) with the default branch (commit c29ecae, 2026-11-11) read for unreleased work such as SSH machines: README, docs/, HACKING.md, assets/help.txt and corgi-skill.md, CLI help, provider adapters, release scripts and crash reporting. tals/corgi has no GitHub releases and its only other public repository, corgi-omarchy, is an empty distribution mirror. Screenshot: fallback, first-party localization capture docs/images/localization/ru-review.png.

locations.result: No GitHub releases; only test/* tags. Releases are served from the signed corgi.computer stable channel.
Default branch documents SSH machine profiles (corgi machine add) not in the stable release; no dated promise.
Issues are the feedback channel; no dated roadmap was found.

gaps: No public roadmap file; default-branch features (SSH machines, hero GIF) were not treated as shipped.
